1.title: Understand waste streams and remediation
1.intro: Waste comes as household, business, construction and hazardous streams. Remediation cleans contaminated land or water.
pts: Know the hierarchy: reduce, reuse, recycle, recover, dispose.
Measure a stream: tonnes, composition, sources.
Identify buyers for recovered materials.
Pick a niche: construction waste, organics, e-waste, site clean-up.
Sort a sample into wood, metal, drywall, plastics and organics, and weigh each.
Find who buys each recovered material and what contamination limit they set.
Estimate haul distance, because long distances can erase the value of a material.
1.ex: A building site produces 60 t of waste; sorting could divert 70%, which is 42 t, leaving 18 t for landfill. If disposal costs 100 per tonne, diverting 42 t avoids 4,200, before the cost of sorting.
1.act: Sample and weigh a waste stream.

2.title: Know environmental and handling rules
pts: Provincial approvals are required for waste handling, transport and processing.
Hazardous waste needs manifests and licensed carriers.
Contaminated sites follow assessment and clean-up standards with qualified professionals.
Worker safety training and protective gear are mandatory.
Learn that the definition of hazardous waste varies by province; check the provincial rule.
Keep a training record for each worker, with date and topic.
For contaminated sites, require an assessment report from a qualified professional before work starts.
2.ex: Row: 'Haul hazardous waste | provincial environment ministry | licence and manifest | each load | manifest copies'. A second row: 'Operate a transfer site | provincial environment ministry | approval | before opening | approval letter'. Date each source.

3.title: Plan collection, sorting and treatment
pts: Route collection; sort at source if possible.
Design the sorting line and storage.
Test contamination levels.
Record every load.
Place labelled bins where waste is made, using pictures as well as words.
Size storage for a week of peak flow and keep fire separation between piles.
Weigh the contaminants in ten sample loads.
3.ex: Contamination is 18% in mixed loads and 6% with source sorting. In a 50 t load that is 9 t versus 3 t, so source sorting removes 6 t of contamination.

4.title: Cost per tonne and revenue
pts: Costs: collection, labour, equipment, disposal.
Revenue: collection fee, gate fee, material sales.
Margin per tonne.
Break-even.
Work out cost per tonne from trucks, fuel, labour and tipping fees divided by tonnes handled.
List revenue lines: collection fees, gate fees and material sales.
Test a price fall, since recovered-material prices change.
4.ex: Price 180 per tonne; cost 120; margin 60; fixed cost 540,000 a year gives 540,000 / 60 = 9,000 t. If the price falls 10% to 162, margin is 42 and break-even rises to 540,000 / 42 = about 12,857 t. Teaching figures in CAD.
4.act: Build a cost sheet with price fall.

5.title: Operate safely and measure
pts: Weigh in and out.
Daily safety briefing.
Spill kits and drills.
Report diversion rate.
Weigh every load and keep a scale ticket with date, vehicle and weight.
Hold a daily briefing on hazards, protective gear, who is on site and exits.
Compute diversion rate as diverted tonnes divided by total tonnes.
5.ex: This month 400 t came in and 272 t were diverted, so the rate is 272 / 400 = 68%. Last month's rate was 61%. The change is 7 percentage points; write the cause.

6.title: Win contracts and partners
pts: Municipal and commercial tenders.
References.
Certified reporting.
Track funnel.
Read each tender for scoring weights, mandatory forms and reporting duties.
Prepare references that show outcomes such as tonnes diverted.
Price with a margin and a fuel-escalation clause.
6.ex: Funnel: 15 bids, 4 shortlists, 2 wins. Shortlist rate is 4 / 15 = 27%, win rate from shortlist is 2 / 4 = 50%, and overall 2 / 15 = 13%.

7.title: Manage contamination, community and liability risk
pts: Odour, noise and traffic complaints.
Fire at storage.
Financial assurance.
Insurance.
Keep a complaint log with date, type, response and closing date.
Reduce fire risk with separate piles, temperature checks, extinguishers and fire-truck access.
Check that insurance covers pollution and check the provincial financial-assurance rule.
7.ex: Risk: 'Storage fire | 2 x 5 | spacing, detection | site lead | monthly'. The score is 2 x 5 = 10; low likelihood but severe impact, so controls are checked monthly.

8.title: Pilot a stream
pts: 60 days.
Measure diversion, cost per tonne.
Stop rule: contamination over 15% means fix.
Plan scale.
Choose one stream, such as clean wood from three sites.
Weigh in, sort and weigh out, and keep the tickets.
Report results to the buyer and ask what they want improved.
8.ex: Contamination 8%: in 25 t that is 2 t. The stop line of 15% would be 3.75 t (25 x 0.15), so the pilot passes and you proceed to plan scale.

quiz: The provincial environment authority, under the provincial rule.
Clean-up cost if the operator fails.
Spills and fires need quick response.
